_why:
Asaas validates the charge SEMANTICALLY, not structurally — and it SHORT-CIRCUITS on the first error, instead of returning the whole list.

Proven against the real sandbox: a POST /v3/payments with an empty body returns ONE error only —
  {"errors":[{"code":"invalid_customer","description":"Customer inválido ou não informado."}]}

While `required` was in the schema, Elysia rejected the body BEFORE the handler and returned 17 TypeBox errors, in English ("Expected string", "Expected union value"), that no Asaas client would ever see. It is the worst kind of infidelity: the developer writes the error handling against our format and breaks in production.

Taking `required` out sends the validation back to the handler — which is where it lives in Asaas: in the right order (customer → billingType → dueDate → value), stopping at the first error, with the right messages.

Bonus: it also fixes the defect Track H noted. `value` was mandatory even in an INSTALLMENT charge through POST /v3/payments, where the amount comes in `totalValue` or `installmentValue` — exactly the same defect overlay 003 fixed in the InstallmentSaveRequestDTO, on the other end.

`remoteIp`, which the card variant marks as required, is still required by the handler — but ONLY when the body actually carries a card. Requiring it for a bank slip would make the simulator stricter than the real API.
